_como_usar: Copiar pra conteudo/carrosseis/<N>_<nome>/_scripts/prompts.json. Cada imagem nova ganha um número novo em images (nunca reaproveitar número: a versão anterior fica). Cena em inglês, curta, dizendo o objeto, onde ele está apoiado, que fica na metade de baixo e 'Nothing else'. Use base_alto quando o objeto precisa subir (postes, geladeira): parede só nos 30% de cima. Rodar: python3 .claude/skills/frase/scripts/gen.py conteudo/carrosseis/<N>_<nome> 1
base: black-and-white editorial fine-art photograph, desaturated, high contrast, fine film grain. SQUARE 1:1 aspect ratio. Minimal composition, like a museum object photograph. The ENTIRE UPPER HALF of the image is a plain, smooth, light plaster wall, bright and empty, fading to near-white at the top edge for clean compositing. Everything that matters sits in the lower half of the frame; nothing enters from above. No text, no words, no logos, no gradients, no added color, no stock photo look, no clutter, no people, no face.
base_alto: black-and-white editorial fine-art photograph, desaturated, high contrast, fine film grain. SQUARE 1:1 aspect ratio. Minimal composition, like a museum object photograph. No text, no words, no logos, no gradients, no added color, no stock photo look, no clutter, no people, no face.

images.scene: A short brick wall under construction, about six rows high, built with Brazilian orange ceramic hollow bricks (tijolo baiano) and grey mortar, standing on a concrete floor against the plain plaster wall; the wall is visibly leaning to one side, more off at the top than at the base, and a yellow spirit level rests on the top row with its bubble clearly off center. A mason's trowel lies on the floor beside it. The wall ends well below the middle of the frame. Nothing else. Hard low side light, long shadow.

Close view at floor level: the first row of Brazilian ceramic hollow bricks (tijolo baiano) laid on fresh grey mortar on a concrete floor against the plain plaster wall; the FIRST brick is set slightly crooked and every brick after it follows the same wrong angle, the whole row drifting off a taut string line stretched straight beside it. A mason's trowel with mortar rests next to the first brick. Everything low, in the lower third of the frame. Nothing else. Hard low side light, long shadows.

A taller unfinished brick wall of Brazilian ceramic hollow bricks (tijolo baiano) on a construction floor against the plain plaster wall, about ten rows high, clearly leaning: the bottom row is almost straight, and each row above drifts a little more to the side, so the top is visibly out of plumb. A bucket of mortar and a trowel at its base. The top of the wall ends at about 35% from the top of the frame; nothing hangs from above. Nothing else. Hard side light, long shadow.
